## Objective
- Add playable “Snake Rush” and “Settlement” ads to the existing AdPlay game, which the user says is otherwise finished.

## Requirements
- Build the requested changes without asking clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- For visual checks, save small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px) and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- No implementation decisions made yet.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected the existing game structure, level registry, snake level, UI, and shared utilities.

### Active
- Add “Snake Rush” and “Settlement” as playable ads and integrate them into the game’s level flow.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect remaining level implementations and the startup scripts as needed to follow existing patterns.
2. Implement the two new playable levels and register them in `src/main.js`; update UI copy/counts if needed.
3. Run the game and verify both levels, including a latest small JPEG screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: level registry, progression, stars, results, and home-screen copy.
- `src/levels/snake.js`: existing snake mini-game that may inform Snake Rush.
- `src/levels/squad.js`: example runner-style level implementation.
- `src/util.js`: shared canvas, input, and game-loop utilities.
- `index.html`: home screen and playable-ad shell.
- `styles.css`: app and game presentation.
- `start.sh`: available project startup script.
- `capture.sh`: available screenshot capture script.

## Important Context
- Existing registry contains seven playable levels; `snake` is currently titled “Snake Bites” and uses `src/levels/snake.js`.
- No files were changed. Attempting to read `package.json` returned `File not found: package.json`.

4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
16: - Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
17: - Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

21: - Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
22: - Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
23: - Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

content.text:
<subagent sessionID="ses_e51666c86ffeyz8wN9U9dgD1cH" state="completed">
## Adding a level

- The central registry is `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/main.js` (`LEVELS`, near the top). A new level needs an import from `src/levels/<name>.js` and a registry entry with a unique `id`, sequential `n`, display metadata (`title`, `studio`, `claim`, `icon`, `c1`, `c2`), `hint`, and `mount`. `lowerBetter` is used for scores like move counts.
- Level modules follow `export function mount(root, api)`. They typically clear `root`, create a canvas stage with `createStage(root)` from `src/util.js`, bind touch/keyboard input, run updates via `createLoop`, then return a `destroy()` method that stops the loop and cleans up input and stage resources. See `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/levels/sort.js` for a DOM-plus-canvas example and `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/levels/squad.js` for keyboard and pointer controls.
- Report outcomes through `api.win(stars, score, opts)` or `api.lose(reason)`; the host handles saving and displaying results. Keep cleanup comprehensive because the host calls `destroy()` when leaving or restarting a level.
- `scoreLabel` appears in the registry, but result text is currently formatted by `id` in `formatScore()` and `formatBest()` in `main.js`; add cases there for a new level’s desired score wording. `bestText()` also has special cases for knife and sort.

## Registry, UI, and count updates

- The home cards are generated from `LEVELS` in `renderHome()`, so there is no separate per-level card markup. Total stars, next/continue level, and the final-level result behavior also derive from the registry.
- Several visible counts and descriptions are hard-coded and should be checked when adding a level: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html` has the “7 playable ads” season pill, “Seven” hero copy, and a `/21` star total; `main.js` has the seven-level help text and list of game types. The page description in `index.html` still says “five” even though the current registry has seven.
- Cards use a two-column grid in `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`; the list itself grows automatically.

## Startup and screenshot workflow
